statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail sits in the low band after the U.S. cash open produced a full retracement of its opening advance rather than continuation.
recommendation: Conditions are described as orderly two-way price discovery with decaying implied volatility. A narrow danger window is flagged from 19:00 to 21:00 UTC covering the Friday power hour, the 20:00 UTC cash close and the 21:00 UTC Globex halt before a three-day U.S. weekend.
headline: Nasdaq-100 fully retraces its opening advance, trading 29,534.94 near the session low after a 29,655.22 high, with VIX easing to 14.07 and the 10-year off its 4.812 percent peak
body:
The decisive development since the previous assessment is that the 13:30 UTC cash open has been observed and did not produce continuation. The Nasdaq-100 opened at 29,539.57 against a 29,482.32 previous close, dipped to a session low of 29,516.20, rallied to 29,655.22, stood at 29,622.87 at 14:07 UTC and had traded back to 29,534.94 by 14:26 UTC, up 0.18 percent on the day and roughly nineteen points above its low. The entire opening advance was given back inside the first cash hour. Opening-auction continuation from an already aligned regime is the specific evidence class that has preceded past mean-reversion failures, and it is precisely what did not happen.

The macro trigger remains the August Employment Situation released at 12:30 UTC. Nonfarm payrolls rose 162,000 against a consensus near 55,000, the unemployment rate held at 4.1 percent and average hourly earnings rose 0.3 percent on the month and 3.1 percent on the year. The report lands into a policy debate about a September increase rather than a cut, and market-implied odds of a quarter-point move sit near a coin flip. That is a genuine repricing, but its transmission has been orderly.

Cross-asset evidence supports the benign reading. VIX traded at 14.07, down 1.75 percent from a 14.32 close and inside a 13.80 to 14.33 range, so implied volatility decayed through and after the release rather than expanding. The 10-year yield stood at 4.776 percent, up 1.4 basis points, having retraced from a 4.812 percent session high, and the 2-year at 4.38 percent was up 2.6 basis points, a modest front-end concentration consistent with a policy surprise. West Texas Intermediate fell 2.10 percent to 89.38 dollars as tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz increased, easing rather than escalating the standing supply channel.

Index direction remains divergent rather than aligned: the Nasdaq-100 is higher on the day while the Dow is down 0.54 percent and the S&P 500 down about 0.29 percent, with small caps notably weaker under the hike repricing. Conflicting cross-index direction raises uncertainty, and Stress is held in the elevated band to reflect it, but divergence is the opposite of the aligned one-way structure that would raise Tail. Volatility decay, a deep observed retracement and unaligned cross-assets together justify moving Tail back into the low band.

The remaining structure of the day is mechanical rather than macro. No further U.S. macro release is scheduled today. The U.S. cash close falls at 20:00 UTC and CME Globex equity futures halt at 21:00 UTC for the weekend, so the final sixteen hours of the horizon carry no live price path at all. The narrow danger window from 19:00 to 21:00 UTC covers the Friday power hour and the closing auction, where position adjustment before a three-day weekend concentrates into a short span. U.S. markets are closed on Monday 7 September for Labor Day, and the next scheduled catalysts are the Producer Price Index on 10 September and the Consumer Price Index on 11 September ahead of the 16 September policy decision.

The principal limitation is that only one cash hour has been observed since the open. A decisive break of the 29,516 to 29,655 band accompanied by shallow pullbacks and repeated extension would invalidate this reading, and the danger window is held across the late session rather than closed on the strength of a single orderly hour.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours divide into three phases. Through the 3 September U.S. session the assessment tracked a technology-led advance that lifted Tail into the watch band between 15:00 and 18:00 UTC as trend-up structure developed, with the Nasdaq-100 closing 1.16 percent higher at 29,482.32. Overnight the mode returned to normal and Tail fell to a trough of 12 as the advance consolidated without extension. From 04:00 UTC the scores drifted higher hour by hour as pre-payrolls positioning built, peaking at Tail 24 and Stress 76 in the 12:00 UTC slot immediately after the release, when the surprise was verified but no post-release price path was yet observable. The 13:00 UTC slot eased to Tail 20 as futures gave back the release spike ahead of the cash open.
outlookSummary: The horizon splits cleanly at the weekend halt. Through the remaining cash session the modelled path decays into the low band on the condition that the 29,516 to 29,655 band continues to contain trade and no repeated extension after failed retracements appears, reaching its trough around 17:00 UTC when pre-holiday midday liquidity is thinnest. A lift back into the watch band is modelled for the 19:00 and 20:00 UTC hours, where Friday power-hour flows, the cash close and gap risk before a three-day weekend concentrate position adjustment into a narrow span. From the 21:00 UTC CME Globex halt the final sixteen hours carry no live price path, so the modelled scores fall to a floor that reflects a closed market rather than an assessment of structure, with confidence decaying slowly as Friday's verified evidence ages. Beyond the horizon, U.S. markets are closed on Monday 7 September for Labor Day, and the next scheduled catalysts are PPI on 10 September and CPI on 11 September ahead of the 16 September policy decision.
